claims.claim: Amendment 13 to Israel's Privacy Protection Law came into force August 14, 2025. It requires informed, freely given, granular, mostly explicit consent (no bundled/pre-ticked); uploading phone/email lists for Meta Custom Audiences or Google Customer Match needs documented consent for that specific use; mandatory privacy protection officers (DPO) for some organizations (enforcement grace period ended Oct 31, 2025); stricter data-broker and transparency rules; expanded PPA enforcement with large fines.

With the enactment of Amendment 13 to the Protection of Privacy Law, 5741-1981, the country has introduced a comprehensive overhaul of its privacy framework. claims.claim: Israel's Spam Law (Section 30A of the Communications Law / סעיף 30א) governs commercial messaging: sending an advertisement by SMS, email, or automated call requires prior opt-in consent, the message must identify the sender and carry the word 'פרסומת' with a working opt-out, and a violation carries statutory damages of up to about 1,000 NIS per message without proof of harm. This is distinct from Amendment 13 (which governs the data/list, not the messaging).
